title: Course orientation · distributed computing scope
summary: Use the Lec0 overview as a short scope boundary before the three numbered lecture weeks.
objectives: Separate course orientation from lecture derivations
Identify the scale, communication, coordination, and failure dimensions
State what evidence a distributed-system claim requires

sections.title: Course boundary · why distributed systems
sections.body: Lec0 frames distributed computing as a response to scale and failure: data can outgrow one machine, and hardware or networks can fail. This is orientation for the three numbered lecture weeks; the detailed models and algorithms begin in Lec1.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The overview sets the boundary for later claims without replacing the derivations in Lec1, Lec2, or Lec3.

sections.title: Evidence standard · how to measure
sections.body: For a project claim, state the workload, workers, partitioning, communication, coordination, and failure assumptions. Lec0 names project directions, but later lecture derivations remain the source for consistency, ordering, and algorithmic guarantees.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Project work becomes learnable when the claim, measurement, system setting, and failure assumption are explicit.

examples.title: Compare two distributed runs
steps: Hold the workload and expected output fixed.
Record workers, partitioning, bytes moved, and coordination waits.
Compare throughput and tail latency under the same failure assumptions.
Attribute a regression to computation, communication, skew, or recovery before changing the design.
examples.answer: A useful comparison explains the measured change using the system conditions, not only a single runtime number.

contrastDrills.prompt: Two runs perform the same arithmetic, but one moves ten times more data between workers. Which cost changed?
contrastDrills.explanation: The arithmetic is unchanged; data movement and message transfer changed the communication cost.
contrastDrills.misconception: Name the ordering, time, or communication boundary before choosing.

math.explanation: Use this as a reporting model: separate useful computation from network movement and coordination waits before interpreting a distributed runtime.
math.name: Distributed cost dimensions
math.purpose: Use it to report useful work separately from network movement and coordination overhead.

criticalQuestions.prompt: Which conditions must stay fixed before comparing two distributed runs?
criticalQuestions.angle: Separate the workload and expected result from the system variables being measured.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: Keep the workload, algorithm, expected output, and correctness criterion fixed. Then record workers, partitioning, communication, coordination, and failure assumptions so the comparison is interpretable.

criticalQuestions.prompt: What evidence separates communication overhead from computation time?
criticalQuestions.angle: Look for bytes moved, network time, coordination waits, and useful-work measurements rather than one total runtime.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: Report compute time alongside bytes moved, network time, serialization, coordination waits, and skew. A total runtime alone cannot identify which system cost changed.
